claim.markdown_says: page 606: '#### 14.9.1.1 General' and '#### 14.9.1.2 General formats'; page 607: '## 14.9.1.3 Syntax rules' and '## 14.9.1.4 General rules' (source lines 25246, 25270, 25285)
claim.why_it_matters: Sibling clauses land two levels apart, and 14.9.1.3 / 14.9.1.4 end up at '##' -- the SAME level as their great-grandparent '## 14.9 Statements' -- so ACCEPT's syntax rules and general rules detach from the ACCEPT statement in every generated table of contents and in any tool that walks the heading tree. 14.9.1.1/14.9.1.2 are the only two '####' headings among all 204 14.9.x.y headings in the file, so this pair is a localized anomaly, not the document convention.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds; no content is missing or altered. 1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind label 'missing-heading' is factually wrong. Both headings are present in the markdown verbatim, with correct clause numbers, correct titles, and correct anchors: line 25270 '' + '## 14.9.1.3 Syntax rules', line 25285 '' + '## 14.9.1.4 General rules'. All six syntax rules and both FORMAT 1 general rules under them transcribe faithfully against the rendered page. The sole difference is the count of '#' characters. 2) THE PDF CARRIES NO LEVEL EVIDENCE. I rendered page 606 at 300dpi. '14.9 Statements', '14.9.1 ACCEPT statement', '14.9.1.1 General' and '14.9.1.2 General formats' are ALL printed in the identical bold face at the identical point size -- the document does not typographically distinguish depth at any level. Page 607 prints '14.9.1.3 Syntax rules' and '14.9.1.4 General rules' in that same single heading style. So the claim's premise ('printed at the same typographic level as their siblings') is true only trivially: every heading of every depth in this standard is printed at the same typographic level. Hierarchy in the PDF is conveyed ONLY by the clause number, and the markdown reproduces those numbers exactly. There is no PDF fact that the markdown contradicts. 3) THE CLAIM'S DECISIVE STATISTIC IS MISREAD AND POINTS AT THE WRONG PAIR. Of the 204 '14.9.x.y' headings: 162 are '###', 40 are '##', 2 are '####'. The plurality convention is '###', not '##'. More importantly, the immediate parent is '### 14.9.1 ACCEPT statement' (line 25225), so '####' is the CORRECT relative nesting for 14.9.1.1/14.9.1.2 -- page 606 is the well-formed pair, and the claim nominates it as the anomaly. 4) IT IS SYSTEMIC PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE, NOT A PAGE-607 DEFECT. Within section 14.9 alone, 40 of the 102 '.3 Syntax rules' / '.4 General rules' headings sit at '##'. The very next statement repeats the pattern identically: '## 14.9.2 ADD statement' (25457), '### 14.9.2.1' (25460), '### 14.9.2.2' (25465), then '## 14.9.2.3 Syntax rules' (25525) and '## 14.9.2.4 General rules' (25546) -- children at the same level as their own parent. Document-wide there are 592 such level inversions among 2082 numbered headings (28%). The mechanical cause is the page-chunked conversion: 505 of 591 numbered headings that are FIRST on their page sit at '##', versus 213 of 1491 that are not. Line 25270 '## 14.9.1.3' is precisely the first heading after the '## Page 607' marker. Note also that '## Page NNN' is itself emitted at '##', so '##' is literally the page-furniture level and any heading-tree walker must already account for it. Meaning is unchanged: the same clause numbers, titles, rules and anchors are present. This falls squarely under the reject criteria -- page-break furniture / formatting artifact of the transcription pipeline, not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. Any fix belongs to a single document-wide heading-level normalization pass over all 592 inversions, not to a page-607 reconciliation entry.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. Both headings are present, correctly numbered, correctly titled and correctly anchored on page 607; no text differs from the PDF. The only difference is markdown heading depth ('##' rather than a depth nested under '### 14.9.1 ACCEPT statement'). The PDF cannot adjudicate depth at all -- page 606 shows 14.9, 14.9.1, 14.9.1.1 and 14.9.1.2 printed in one identical bold face at one identical size, so depth is expressed solely by the clause number, which the markdown preserves exactly. The claim also inverts its own evidence: '###' is the plurality for 14.9.x.y (162 of 204) and '####' is the CORRECT nesting under '### 14.9.1', so the page-606 pair it calls anomalous is the well-formed one. Far from localized, the pattern is a document-wide artifact of page-chunked conversion: 592 heading-level inversions across 2082 numbered headings, 40 of them among 14.9's own Syntax/General rules headings, reproduced verbatim one statement later at '## 14.9.2.3' / '## 14.9.2.4'; 505 of 591 first-on-page numbered headings are flattened to '##', and '## 14.9.1.3' is exactly the first heading after the '## Page 607' marker. If addressed at all, this belongs to one global heading-level normalization pass, not a page-607 finding.
